summary: The noun marks the angle where sides meet in a structure, including a city wall. Ezekiel uses a related passive form of the four small courts at the corners of the outer court.

senses.definition: A place where sides meet or a wall changes direction.

evidence.note: The two paired frames are joined at the two corners of the dwelling.
Baruch’s section of wall starts at the angle and runs to the entrance of Eliashib’s house.
Ezekiel finds a smaller court in each of the four corners of the outer court.

senses.definition: Situated at the corners of a larger enclosure.

evidence.note: The description gives the same dimensions for all four courts just located at the corners.

note: The four-court arrangement gives the passive form its probable meaning. Its only occurrence is the final word of Ezekiel 46:22. A historical connection between the architectural and scraping terms remains uncertain.
